rows.question: Which district has the highest poverty rate?
rows.answer: Nyamagabe District had the highest headcount poverty rate at 51.4% in EICV7 2023/24. Its confidence interval was 45.1% to 57.7%.

rows.question: What is the poverty rate in the City of Kigali?
rows.answer: The headcount poverty rate in the City of Kigali was 9.1% in EICV7 2023/24. Its 95% confidence interval was 7.0% to 11.1%, with a standard error of 1.1 percentage points.

rows.question: Which 5 districts have the lowest poverty rates?
rows.answer: In EICV7 2023/24, the five districts with the lowest headcount poverty rates were Nyarugenge at 6.8%, Kicukiro at 6.9%, Gasabo at 11.1%, Gicumbi at 13.3%, and Kirehe at 14.2%. These are survey estimates: their confidence intervals were 4.4% to 9.2%, 4.3% to 9.5%, 7.4% to 14.7%, 9.2% to 17.4%, and 10.1% to 18.4%, respectively.

rows.question: What was Rwanda's population in the 2022 census?
rows.answer: Rwanda’s resident population was 13,246,394 in the Census 2022 (RPHC5).

rows.question: What is the population density of Kicukiro?
rows.answer: Kicukiro had a population density of 2,944 people per km² in the Census 2022 (RPHC5).

rows.question: Compare poverty and electricity access across Western Province districts.
rows.answer: EICV7 Main Indicators 2023/24 shows poverty was highest in Rusizi at 44.2% and lowest in Nyabihu at 20.4% among Western Province districts. Electricity as the main lighting source ranged from 60.6% in Nyabihu to 78.8% in Rusizi. The other districts were Nyamasheke, 42.7% poverty and 74.3% electricity; Rutsiro, 40.8% and 71.1%; Rubavu, 38.8% and 74.5%; Karongi, 38.2% and 67.8%; and Ngororero, 30.2% and 68.0%.

rows.question: Which districts have poverty above 40% and the lowest internet access at home?
rows.answer: In EICV7 2023/24, Nyamagabe had the lowest household internet access at home among districts with poverty above 40%: 9.2%, while its poverty rate was 51.4%. The other qualifying districts, ordered by internet access at home, were Nyanza (15.0%; poverty 43.3%), Rutsiro (16.2%; 40.8%), Nyamasheke (25.6%; 42.7%), Gisagara (28.5%; 45.6%), and Rusizi (44.1%; 44.2%).

rows.question: How does health insurance coverage in Nyanza compare to the national average?
rows.answer: In Census 2022, health-insurance coverage was 93.4% in Nyanza, compared with 97.3% nationally, a difference of 3.9 percentage points. In EICV7 2023/24, Nyanza was 82.3% versus 85.3% nationally, a 3.0-point difference; the Nyanza estimate has a 78.5% to 86.1% confidence interval.

rows.question: What share of households in Rwanda use electricity for lighting?
rows.answer: Census 2022 reports that 47.0% of private households in Rwanda used electricity from the grid as their main lighting source. EICV7 2023/24 reports 72.0% of households used electricity as their main lighting source, with a confidence interval of 71.1% to 73.0%. The figures differ because they come from different surveys and years.

rows.question: What is the unemployment rate in Rwanda?
rows.answer: Rwanda’s unemployment rate was 13.4% in Q2 2026, according to the Labour Force Survey Q2 2026.

rows.question: What is the HIV prevalence in Musanze?
rows.answer: The available NISR tables do not provide HIV prevalence for Musanze. HIV outcomes are covered by the Rwanda Demographic and Health Survey (DHS), available through the NISR microdata catalogue at http://microdata.statistics.gov.rw/.

rows.question: Who will win the next election?
rows.answer: I cannot predict who will win the next election. Election outcomes and political opinions are outside the scope of NISR statistical tables.
